lead: St. Petersburg is surrounded by water on three sides, and its older homes sit low. In 2024, Helene's surge and Milton's winds hit the city two weeks apart.
risk: storm surge, hurricane wind damage and aging plumbing
why: Hurricane Helene passed far offshore in September 2024, but its surge pushed water from Tampa Bay and the Gulf into low neighborhoods. Shore Acres, Snell Isle and other waterfront areas flooded, and thousands of homes took on water. Two weeks later, Hurricane Milton brought wind and heavy rain across the city. Its winds tore much of the fabric roof off Tropicana Field and damaged homes across town.

Age is a big factor here. About 70% of St. Petersburg homes were built before 1980, many on low ground with cast-iron drains and old supply lines. Older homes that flooded may now face rules on raising or rebuilding them. Summer humidity also means that wet drywall and carpet can start growing mold within a day or two of a leak or flood.
image_alt: Roofer working on a red tile roof
image_caption: After Milton, many tile and shingle roofs across St. Petersburg needed repairs.
problems: Shore Acres, Snell Isle, Coquina Key
Pre-1980 homes in Kenwood, Crescent Lake
tips: Know your evacuation zone; surge is the deadliest part of a storm.
Buy flood insurance early; it usually takes 30 days to start.
Have old cast-iron drains scoped with a camera.
Photograph each room before hurricane season for your claim.
areas: Calls come from Old Northeast, Snell Isle, Shore Acres, Kenwood, Crescent Lake, Historic Roser Park, Placido Bayou and Coquina Key, plus Gulfport, Pinellas Park and Treasure Island.

faq.q: Does my St. Petersburg home policy cover storm surge?
faq.a: No. Surge and rising water need a flood policy from the NFIP or a private insurer. Your home policy may cover wind damage and rain that gets in through a damaged roof, usually with a separate hurricane deductible. Many St. Petersburg homes need both policies.
